slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Not determined. The single .sav sample has 0 active (non-fill) byte ranges, so no slot boundary, copy, or generation/sequence counter can be observed.

caller_chains.trigger_context: BIOS software_interrupt(0xC) (CpuFastSet) driven audio/stream-buffer mixing engine; cursor/offset fields at param_1+0x14..0x8d of a per-channel struct.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced every caller/callee edge for this address in ghidra/callgraph.json, confirmed 0 edges leave this 18-function set, and read each function body in ghidra/decompiled.c to classify all memory references: all are EWRAM/IWRAM audio-channel state, none address 0x0D000000-0x0E00FFFF (EEPROM/SRAM/Flash) or 0x040000D4 (DMA3). Ruled out as save-related; no ram_fields_updated map to a save struct.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Software floating-point arithmetic library (unpack/pack, add/sub, multiply, divide, compare, int-to-float, 64-bit multiply helper), called from the audio cluster above for tick/time-ratio math.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Same method as the audio cluster: 0 cross-cluster edges in ghidra/callgraph.json, and every memory/register reference in ghidra/decompiled.c is local stack/float-record state, never a save address. Ruled out as save-related.

open_questions: Which GBA save protocol does this title actually use (plain 32KB SRAM, Flash with 0x5555/0x2AAA command sequence, or EEPROM via DMA3)? The SRAM_F_V103 SDK tag string is a hint only, not confirmed by any traced I/O code.

No save-write or save-read function was captured by the trace behind ghidra/decompiled.c (0 MMIO seeds in ghidra/save_related_functions.c). A new trace that spans an actual in-game save/load is required to surface the real driver, serialization, and checksum routines.

The one .sav sample (saves/cap-00-future-0.sav) is entirely 0xFF with 0 active byte ranges, so no magic signature, checksum, slot boundary, or field offset can be derived from content alone. A non-blank capture (ideally several, from different save slots/characters/progress points) is required.
states/ is empty; no paired pre-save/post-save .ss states exist yet to diff EWRAM/IWRAM and locate the in-RAM save staging struct independent of static code analysis.

Is the 32768-byte file size a property of the real cartridge save chip, or a fixed-size backing file allocated by the capture tooling regardless of actual save-chip type? Needs cross-checking against the ROM's actual declared save type once driver code is found.
